items.text: Day one of the US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended without announced agreements; [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] called it constructive, saying delegations discussed parameters for humanitarian steps, prisoner releases and the substance of long-term security guarantees. A second day opened on 11 Nov with a trilateral session, followed by Ukrainian meetings with French, German, British and Italian national security advisers.
items.notes: Outcome of day two not yet reported at time of logging. Watch item W-261025-04 (check date today).

items.text: China's [[p:Ministry of Commerce (China)|Commerce Ministry]] extended its suspension of export controls on rare earths and other critical minerals by two months, to 10 Jan, and its finance ministry kept the 24% retaliatory tariff on US goods suspended (a 10% levy stays). The US suspended its Section 301 action on China's maritime and logistics sectors and extended 178 tariff exclusions. The truce had been due to lapse on 10 Nov, a week before [[p:Donald Trump]] and [[p:Xi Jinping]] are expected to meet at APEC in Shenzhen.
items.notes: Short extension keeps leverage for both sides into the APEC meeting.

items.text: Taiwan's defence minister [[p:Wellington Koo|Wellington Koo (politician, born 1958)]] confirmed that the [[p:Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning|Liaoning]] carrier group and formations from other theatre commands are running "area denial" drills in the western Pacific, which Beijing has not declared. National Security Council chief [[p:Joseph Wu]] said on 3 Nov that more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard ships were operating around Taiwan, the South China Sea and the Pacific. [[p:Institute for the Study of War|ISW]] and AEI analysts assess the deployment as an unannounced rehearsal of isolating Taiwan; Beijing earlier called the carrier's Pacific training routine.
items.notes: Ship deployment confirmed by Taiwan officials; 'isolation rehearsal' reading is ISW/AEI analysis. Taiwan local elections on 28 Nov.

items.text: Efforts to arrange a [[p:Sanae Takaichi]]–[[p:Xi Jinping]] meeting at APEC in Shenzhen (18–19 Nov) have stalled, Kyodo reports, with Beijing still refusing dialogue over Takaichi's November 2025 remarks on a Taiwan contingency. A Chinese source quoted says Japan may be the only major participant without talks with Xi; Tokyo says it will keep trying and a brief handshake is seen as the realistic goal. The anniversary of the remarks on 7 Nov passed with no thaw.
items.outlet: Central News Agency (citing Kyodo); The Japan Times
items.notes: Chinese-language CNA report translating Kyodo; paraphrased.

items.text: North Korea fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the East Sea, South Korea's military said; state media described the launch as a test of a newly designed air-defence missile system, testing new materials and guidance, alongside an unidentified "fire strike" drill. Types and number were not disclosed. A day earlier [[p:Kim Jong Un]] inspected a new warship under construction at Nampho.

[[p:Kim Yo Jong]] said in KCNA statements that Pyongyang has no need to sit down with Washington until it drops its "hostile policy", including denuclearisation demands and joint drills, and called US attribution of the multi-billion-dollar Binance hack to North Korea part of that policy; she also said dialogue remained one option. Since the 3 Nov US midterms, state media have been silent and Seoul officials see no groundwork for a Trump–Kim meeting at APEC.
items.notes: Statement confirmed via KCNA as reported by Korean press; the 'no groundwork' point is government sources quoted by News1.

items.text: Manila is preparing the [[e:2026 ASEAN Summits|49th ASEAN Summit]] for 16–18 Nov at the Philippine International Convention Center; [[p:Donald Trump]] is due on 16 Nov before flying to APEC in Shenzhen, and Chinese premier [[p:Li Qiang]] rather than Xi is expected. [[p:Bongbong Marcos|Ferdinand Marcos Jr.]] wants progress on a South China Sea code of conduct, but the July 2026 target lapsed and he has said a November deal is very hard; scope and legal force remain unresolved.
items.notes: Exact dates vary across reports (15–17, 16–18 Nov); security measures run 15–18 Nov. Li Qiang attendance per Inquirer headline only.

items.text: At the close of [[p:Yoon Suk Yeol]]'s appeal trial for leading an insurrection, special prosecutors again sought the death penalty; Yoon called his December 2024 martial law a "message" about government paralysis and denied plans to blockade the National Assembly. The Seoul High Court will rule on 26 Jan 2027; he was sentenced to life in February 2026.

The Senate impeachment trial of Vice President [[p:Sara Duterte]] resumed on 9 Nov on the one remaining article, unexplained wealth, with defence witnesses questioned over gaps between her asset declarations and tax records; sessions run through 23 Nov. Her father [[p:Rodrigo Duterte]]'s ICC trial opens in The Hague on 30 Nov, and she has asked to visit him in December.

The [[p:Arakan Army]] attacked the Shwemingan naval base on the northern edge of Sittwe, claiming heavy junta losses, as the military reportedly masses about 7,000 troops in a shrinking perimeter and counter-attacks on nearby Ngapyi Island. Junta airstrikes hit a hospital in Kawlin (4 Nov) and a school in Kani (7 Nov), local outlets report.
items.outlet: Ayeyarwaddy Times; People's Spring (via Burma Coup Resistance Notes); The Irrawaddy
items.notes: Battlefield claims from AA-aligned and resistance outlets; not independently verified. Compilation of local reports, translated.

items.text: Washington published a Myanmar country strategy that includes engagement with the military-led government and an "inclusive peace" agenda; the opposition [[p:National Unity Government of Myanmar|National Unity Government]] warned against legitimising the junta.
items.notes: Single compiled source; State Department document not seen directly.

items.text: Thai PM [[p:Anutin Charnvirakul]] warned Myanmar's junta and sent ground troops and F-16s to the border after junta bombing of a Karen camp damaged buildings on the Thai side and the junta reportedly threatened businesses trading with Karen-held areas.
items.outlet: Karen Information Center; Myanmar Pressphoto Agency (via Burma Coup Resistance Notes)

items.text: Cambodia revoked 18 casino licences linked to [[p:Prince Group]] and froze over $300 million in accounts, as the US Treasury imposed a third round of sanctions on the group's network, including an airline and an insurer, four people and 41 entities.
items.outlet: Khmer Times; CamboJA News; The Straits Times

items.text: Chinese foreign minister [[p:Wang Yi]] hosted informal talks in Beijing between Cambodia's and Thailand's foreign ministers on the sidelines of a Lancang–Mekong meeting; Beijing called them constructive, while Bangkok says the border stays closed and normal ties will not resume for now.

Students and activists scuffled with police near Tugu Tani in central Jakarta on Heroes' Day, protesting alleged corruption, the handling of Kalimantan forest fires and food poisoning in the free-meals programme; police prepared for 74 gatherings and said calm returned. [[p:Prabowo Subianto]] says the meals programme will be improved, not scrapped.
Vietnam's leader [[p:Tô Lâm]] began a visit to Japan focused on AI, semiconductors and nuclear power cooperation.
items.notes: Exact start date not confirmed from full text.

items.text: The [[p:Sanae Takaichi]] government announced an emergency cyber-defence package and wants tougher cybersecurity laws as attacks surge.
